newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-FIFA CALLS FOR WORLD CUP FENCES TO BE SCRAPPED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA CALLS FOR WORLD CUP FENCES TO BE SCRAPPED.

text.p: World soccer's governing body FIFA said on Friday France should pull down perimeter fences at its World Cup venues in response to this week's stadium tragedy in Guatemala.
"Fences are for animals and prisoners -- not football fans," FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said. "I believe that all the fences for the World Cup in France should be taken down."
Up to 82 people died and at least 147 were injured when an avalanche of fans tumbled down seats and a flight of stairs at a World Cup qualifying match between Guatemala and Costa Rica on Wednesday.
Many died crushed against the chainlink fence separating the stands from the pitch in the worst soccer stadium disaster in World Cup history.
Blatter said FIFA had been working for the last few weeks on dropping plans to have fences in France, which is due to host the finals of soccer's premier tournament in 1998.
There was no fencing at this year's European championship in England, and no major crowd trouble inside the grounds.
FIFA said Guatemala's next qualifying match against Trinidad and Tobago -- originally scheduled for next Friday -- had been postponed indefinitely, as had the aborted match against Costa Rica.
"All other matches will proceed as scheduled, including a game between the United States and Guatemala in the United States on November 3," FIFA spokesman Andreas Herren said.
